The original localhost:4000 paper body was unreachable at reconstruction time, so this is rebuilt from those sources and the built code — not a byte-copy of the lost original. Canonical ledger: the hyperquiz-epic task tree on guerrilla.

A live-quiz game running on Barkpark itself. A projector shows the spectacle, phones are the input, and Studio is the authoring desk — the host live-edits a question mid-game and every connected screen updates in under a second.

items.value: Projector / host — /quiz/host/:pin: the question, the choices, and a swarm of live cursors (or, at scale, a heatmap cloud). The spectacle screen.
Phone / player — /quiz/play/:pin: tap a choice, stream a cursor. Anonymous, zero-install, join by PIN.
Studio — the authoring desk: the host live-edits the running quiz and the change propagates to every screen in under a second.

blocks.content: Server-authoritative realtime (a Room GenServer per game, a binary cursor codec, an O(1) heatmap), honest states (loading / empty / error — no fake realtime), styled from the same theme tokens as the rest of Barkpark, and live on guerrilla where merged = deployed.

Scoped away from WoW-scale authoritative simulation (that needs an in-memory game engine; Postgres can't carry game-tick writes). Strength-first: Phoenix presence + WebSocket fan-out + the Barkpark content model + Studio live-edit. The quiz is content; the crowd's cursors and picks render in real time.

The engine already exists on local branch hyperquiz-p1-recovered — 28 commits, +2,952 lines across 35 files, 99 tests green when applied to current main (verified by an actual port attempt 2026-07-09). Priority: landing the stranded engine on main as a Barkpark.Plugin beats any new feature work.
